extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: VQAonline is the first visual question answering (VQA) dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case, sourced from online question answering community forums.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping publicly-available data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange, specifically collecting examples with a natural language question, context, an image, and at least one accepted answer, followed by filtering steps to remove low-quality VQAs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly-available data from Stack Exchange containing a natural language question, a natural language context, an image, and at least one answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Domain experts were hired and trained via one-on-one sessions to introduce the task and instructions. Quality control involved monitoring the time spent on each question to prevent random clicking. Annotators were compensated with a $75 Amazon Gift Card, averaging $26/hour.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Domain experts located in the United States with English proficiency.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may suffer from data contamination during evaluation, as many modern models are pre-trained on Stack Exchange data and might have already been exposed to the VQAonline data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving models on this dataset is expected to positively impact various real-world applications, including community QA platforms, educational tools for children, and virtual assistants.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating and benchmarking Vision and Language Models (VLMs) on authentic visual question answering, improving evaluation metrics for long-form text, and exploring model hallucination issues.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was preprocessed by filtering out visual questions without an accepted answer, those with a score of 0 or less, those with multiple images, those with visual answers, and those with broken image links. Additionally, all images were converted to PNG format for consistency.

name.evidence: Sourced from online question answering community forums, we call it VQAonline.

description.evidence: We introduce the first VQA dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums, we call it VQAonline.

url.evidence: We publicly-share the dataset at: https://vqaonline.github.io/.

license.evidence: We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022, and adhered to all data license restrictions (cc-by-sa 4.0) set forth by Stack Exchange.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: From the Stack Exchange archive, we collected all examples containing four components: a natural language question, a natural language context, an image, and at least one answer.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We hired ten domain experts to represent each of the ten fields (topics)... We provided a one-on-one training session with each domain expert to introduce the task and instructions. Afterwards, we gave each expert our contact information... We also inspected the time each expert spent on each visual question as a proxy for assessing whether the hired domain experts were finishing the task by quickly selecting random options. ... We compensated each domain expert with a $75 Amazon Gift Card, resulting in an average hourly wage of $26/hour.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: The link to the code for our web-based annotation tool is available at https://github.com/VQAonline/VQAonlineVisualization.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: To guarantee English proficiency, as most of our visual questions are written in English, we only accepted experts located in the United States.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Of note, most of these models are believed to be trained on Stack Exchange data and so potentially saw our VQAonline data

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We expect improved models designed for VQAonline can also benefit many other real-world applications including for other community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children [32], virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, as well as visual search and browsing.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We will release our dataset to facilitate further exploration of the hallucination issue in the authentic use cases.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: After removing visual questions without an accepted answer, it resulted in 165,766 visual questions. [...] After removing visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer, we had 119,177 visual questions. Next, after removing visual questions with multiple images, we had 85,573 visual questions. Subsequently, removing visual questions with visual answers, left 65,849 visual questions. [...] Finally, after removing examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link, we got to our final dataset of 64,696 visual questions. For data format consistency, we converted all images to png format.
